title: Central Ops Weekly Updates - 19th Oct
exec_summary:
Snitch Quick (Hritik Kumar): Clocked ₹5.46M GMV across 2,716 orders (11% online share) driven by a 63% Delhi surge post-Lajpat Nagar launch, alongside sharp cut-size reductions and a finalized OND plan; next week centers on diagnosing Gurgaon/Ahmedabad dips, the Yelahanka BTL pilot, and OND tech/expansion roadmaps.

Long Tail (Pratik Agrawal, Tushar Gupta): Delivered ₹1.24 Cr weekly revenue (+9% WoW, 56% target achievement; MTD ₹3.05 Cr at 55%) led by Stores (81%), with immediate focus on deploying selective discounting, redistribution, and festive VM to recover the ₹1.60 Cr MTD Shoe deficit and lagging Online/Marketplace sales.

Experience (Uraza Arif Shamsi): Rolled out RTO/Lost Order cancellation comms, resolved Unfulfillable cancellation/refund breaks, and revamped CX/NPR Slack reporting; next steps focus on automating Lost order refunds, WPR defect bifurcation, and Clickpost NPR configurations.

Distribution (Malhar Murhekar): B2B Forward delivered 1,889 shipments at 81.6% on-time (3.8-day avg) despite steep B2B Reverse drops in same-day pickups (44.64%) and 5-day P2D (10.71%); upcoming focus covers November rulebook revisions, Delhi milk-run feasibility, M Express train cargo routing, and store outwards data automation.

Retail & Store Tech (Mohd Faisal Jamal Kidwai): Deployed Pan-India Replenishment, concluded BORIS training, cleared L1 UAT for Logic ERP Store Inwards APIs, and launched Omni pendency alerts; immediate line items include rolling out Store Inwards, launching Pan-India BORIS, iterating replenishment modules, and configuring DSR tracking.

PLM - WAM (Mohd Faisal Jamal Kidwai, Aniket Khot): Scaled WAM inward adoption to ~86% (2.21L units; North 87%, South 85%), automated Direct RTS allocations, and enhanced QA validation; upcoming focus targets pre-arrival ASN/pre-pack creation and resolving inward bottlenecks from modified or cancelled POs.

Fin Ops (Mohd Faisal Jamal Kidwai): Planned the multi-city BORIS scale-up across Delhi, NCR, Pune, Mumbai, and Hyderabad, with execution currently pending final Finance alignment.

Snitch AI Labs (Sajja Sai Karthik, Hritik Kumar): Closed 0-to-1 NSO scoping, integrated Logic ERP into Recon, and unified Myntra/Flipkart pricing and audit workflows; next steps focus on building Marketplace Recon, aligning NSO with Retail Ops, and measuring the GP and revenue impact of price changes.

RFID (Nitin Manke): Scaled the network to ~108 doors with 7 new store launches while maintaining 83% RFID GRN adherence (1,157 of 1,392 invoices) despite a 28% volume surge, with immediate operational focus on curbing shrinkage risks across 9 chronic 0% stores (primarily in Mumbai/Pune) and executing upcoming NSO rollouts in Nagpur and Jaipur.

Logistics (Iqbal C): Implemented performance based allocation for festive peak loads, completed Lajpat Nagar Quick HLD setup, and optimized critical B2B freight routes (Raipur NDD, Kolkata FTL/Air); next week's focus centers on finalizing M Express train onboarding, redesigning the Control Tower, and resolving persistent Flipkart error order backlogs.

Warehouse (Manish Charan): Sustained 99%+ forward B2C fulfillment across both facilities despite South marketplace label glitches and B2B FIFO-driven SLA drops, while managing 12.8K North NF units and WAM inward bottlenecks; upcoming focus centers on aligning B2B FIFO execution with rulebook metrics, driving aggressive missing stock reductions across South WH1 and WH2.

ERP (Sagar Kumar): Activated key Logic ERP APIs (Store Inward, Journal, Save GR Details) and Mysa integrations, aligned Berrylush GST rates (18% to 5%), while pending leadership sign-off on the OND Godown Transfer customization and vendor resolution for bulk PO imports.

entry.metricsNote:
Clocked ₹5.46M GMV (+0.6% WoW) across 2,716 orders (steady at ~2.7K) at ₹2.06K AOV (+2%), pushing online share to 11% (+1.4 pts) and serviceable city penetration to a 4-week high of 35.1% (+1.7 pts), outperforming non-Quick metros (-38.6%) and RoI (-40.9%) by ~25 pts despite a -13.4% YoY city base. By city:
- Delhi: Quick orders grew 63% WoW, taking share to 20.4%, with the Lajpat Nagar store live since 13 Oct.
- Gurgaon: Quick’s share of the city is the highest at 52.8%, but Quick orders fell 8.4% WoW along with the city (-13.7%).
- Ahmedabad: Quick fell 21% WoW and is the weakest city at 15.8% share.
- Bengaluru (42%) and Hyderabad (29%) were broadly steady.

- Indiranagar from 63% to 30%, Janakpuri from 73% to 49% and CG Road from 61% to 43%.
- Sector 29 from 29% to 19%, HSR from 33% to 26% and Hyderabad MFC from 20% to 16%.

entry.updates:
- Overall Performance: Weekly revenue stood at ₹1.24 Cr (+9.0% WoW), achieving 56% of the ₹2.23 Cr target, with a shortfall of ₹98.37L. MTD revenue reached ₹3.05 Cr (+14.9% YoY), achieving 55% of the ₹5.59 Cr target, leaving a gap of ₹2.54 Cr.
- Channel Performance: Stores continue to lead at ₹60.12L (+13.9% WoW), achieving 81% of weekly target. Online grew 17.5% WoW but remains at 48% achievement, while Marketplace declined 14.6% WoW, achieving just 38% of target. MTD, Stores are at 79%, Online at 45% and Marketplace at 38% achievement.
- Shoes Remain the Largest Concern: Weekly revenue stood at ₹71.59L (+14% WoW), achieving 55% of target. MTD revenue reached ₹1.67 Cr (+19.6% YoY), but achievement remains at 51%, with a shortfall of ~₹1.60 Cr. Shoes contribute 53% of MTD revenue, making recovery critical.
- Perfumes Performance: Weekly revenue stood at ₹38.17L (+2.7% WoW), achieving 61% of target. MTD revenue reached ₹1.01 Cr (+17% YoY), but achievement remains at 64%, indicating significant headroom despite positive growth.
- Other Categories: Bags (43%), Belts (47%) and Sunglasses (55%) remain below weekly targets. Accessories declined 23% YoY MTD, while Bags declined 8%. Trolleys generated ₹8.78L MTD, down 12.6% YoY.
- Key Focus Ahead: Accelerate recovery through selective discounting (25–50% on Shoes, Flat ₹500/₹1,000 on Perfumes), festive VM, targeted CRM and store incentives. Prioritize omnichannel inventory exposure, store redistribution and liquidation of slow-moving inventory, alongside stronger Online and Marketplace execution.

entry.updates:
- WAM adoption has increased significantly across both North and South warehouses, with the majority of inward transactions now being processed through WAM.
- As per the latest inward report, 2,20,891 units have been inwarded through WAM, representing approximately 86% adoption.
- Warehouse-wise WAM adoption:
- North Warehouse: 88,242 units - 87% adoption.
- South Warehouse: 1,32,649 units - 85% adoption.
- Direct RTS adoption completed internally, with allocations now being processed directly through RTS. Allocation communication is currently being sent through the BOT.
- All required Pre-Packs have been created, and ASN creation is being managed proactively. Any missing ASN is now created within 10 minutes of the warehouse team raising the request.
- Winterwear inward has been successfully processed through WAM, expanding its usage across product categories.
- Item Master creation has been made independent within WAM, reducing manual dependencies.
- A confirmation pop-up has been introduced when scanned quantity (PUV) exceeds QA-approved quantity (FI) to improve quantity validation.
- Issue Tracker updated: A new process has been introduced for cases where invoice quantity is lower than QC-passed quantity, reducing manual intervention.
entry.ahead:
- Increase WAM adoption further and target maximum inward processing through WAM across both warehouses.
- Ensure ASN and Pre-Pack creation before shipment arrival to prevent delays at the warehouse.
- Strengthen coordination between the Category, Production, QC and Warehouse teams to ensure all required data is available before inward.
- Track WAM exceptions, manual interventions and warehouse-wise adoption to identify further process improvements.
entry.blockers:
- PO Changed After Goods Arrival: In some cases, the PO number is changed after goods reach the warehouse. Since the QC report is unavailable against the new PO number, the warehouse team is unable to complete the inward.
- Cancelled PO – Goods Received: Vendors are dispatching goods against POs that have already been cancelled. As a result, goods reach the warehouse against an invalid PO, preventing inward processing.
- Cross-Team Dependencies: Timely PO updates, revised QC reports and accurate shipment details are dependent on the Production, Category and other relevant teams.

entry.updates:
- Store Network Expansion: Total operational store count reached ~108 doors following the onboarding of 7 new locations (Trion, EVA, Earth Euphoria, Prozone Mall, Kolhapur, SGS Mall, and City Center Nashik).
- Inbound Inventory Accuracy: Network-wide RFID GRN adoption dropped slightly from 85% to 83%, driven by a 28% WoW surge in volume and the integration of new store go-lives. Out of 1,392 total inbound invoices, 1,157 were processed via RFID while 235 were created manually. Performance remains solid overall, with 50+ stores achieving 100% RFID compliance, including turnaround recoveries at Bannerghatta and HLP Mohali Mall.
- Operational Risks & Escalations: A major operational risk was identified across 9 stores that recorded 0% RFID adoption, processing 100% of inward stock manually. This significantly elevates risk regarding stock discrepancies and inventory shrinkage. Notably, 7 of these doors belong to the Mumbai/Pune regional cluster and have shown zero RFID activity since launch (3-4 weeks back), requiring immediate operational intervention. Additionally, the weekly Global Count stockroom audit export experienced compliance gaps at source.
